question: Does letting the per-target calibration scalar depend on a detector-derived image-quality tercile improve the adopted pipeline?
motivation: The earlier ridge stacking fitted log residuals by L2 (phase 0 shows that alone costs +0.059 pp); a bin-wise MAPE-optimal scalar is the low-variance version of the same hypothesis that point-map statistics flag images where the regression is systematically biased.
design: 3 quality bins by terciles fixed on the four fitting folds; per bin and target the scalar in [0.90,1.10] step 0.0025 minimising MAPE on the fitting folds; applied to the held fold; 'global' variant reproduces the adopted one-scalar pipeline as a code check
pre_specified_decision: candidate if a variant improves the mean by >= 0.03 pp overall and on >= 2 folds with no target worse by > 0.05 pp (3 variants: multiplicity noted)
falsification: deltas >= 0 on most folds mean the regression's bias does not depend on these quality proxies.
